This weekend I refinished a beautiful mahogany easel for my daughter. At first I wanted to Simply sand it by hand preferring not to hear or listen to Electric Tools on the weekends since I deal with them all week long. However that goal went out the window in about 5 minutes into hand sanding.

Instead of working on the bench I sat down on the grass. Might as well be grounded. However grass does stain wood if you sand it on the wood I found this out the hard way. I thought well maybe the the Finish will take it off nope. But I had a great time sanding while sitting on the ground

So I retrieved both my orbital sanders. Brand name DeWalt 1 is hook and loop the other is a square clamp. Now lately I've been preferring the square clamp orbital sander mainly because the cost of the Sandpaper. Before I go any further something to be said about sandpaper.

Guys if you're doing a project buy expensive sandpaper. It does last longer and it's just better. What type of sandpaper? Any 3M product will be decent sandpaper there's all different types and right now I can't think of the one I use for this probably 3M but either way it's not cheap.

Anyway so I like the square sander for other reasons too. 1 it does not leave little circular marks or larger circular marks if you're sanding softwood. The little circular marks may not be noticed from regular distance and it depends upon the project but if you look really close sometimes little pieces of grit create little spirally circle marks. And when the sander is on and you start sanding a piece of wood sometimes the RPM just creates a larger Circle mark anyone who's done this knows what I am talking about.

But here's my point when we sand go with the grain correct but what do you use a square orbital sander what do you do? Well often I go with the grain back and forth back and forth. But this weekend I developed a different technique. And here it is

Instead of going back and forth like you're sanding by hand you twist the orbital sander like you're turning on a knob on a machine you're turning it 90° back and forth medium pressure and watch that wood sand. The difference was noticeable.

Then I use the round orbital for the Finish Grit for this project I went 80 to 120.
